layers.deciding_comparison: Compare the selected task-matched procedures against ECC minimal and no-skill baselines in clean WSL2 Ubuntu x86_64 sessions, using identical pinned models and clients. Include instruction-writing, coding/TDD, debugging and security/testing tasks. Retain discovery traces, loaded sections, concrete findings, instruction conflicts, task success, tokens, elapsed time and installation effort. Repeat on macOS arm64. Add a second procedure source only after measuring its incremental benefit. No verified cross-repository evaluation currently establishes an efficacy winner.
evidence_gaps: Selections are preferred procedure sources based on documented fit and validation infrastructure, not proven repository-wide performance winners.

Selected-source WSL2 and macOS arm64 execution was not verified. Trail’s Ubuntu CI supports Linux suitability; ECC has passing macOS CI, but runner architecture was not established. These instruction procedures do not require the RTX 4090.
Documented installation commands track upstream rather than guaranteeing the reviewed commit pins; installers were not executed on a clean host.
The packet records no completed head-to-head. Matt’s proposed-revision experiment cannot be transferred to its current default branch or used to rank repositories.
Null repository entries were resolved as name aliases of the corresponding official repositories; independent repository identities were not supplied.

Research used 6 web searches and 30 GitHub API calls. Seven page URLs were attempted through the required fetch tool, with zero successful fetches. Primary documents were recovered through GitHub GraphQL, indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search.
The required ctx_fetch_and_index action was rejected: “MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never.” Consequently, the requested page-fetch route could not be completed.
